headline: Nothing has caught on
body: Years in, and there's still no real revenue. Something isn't working, and it's time to actually decide what to do about it.

options.label: Pivot to something else
options.detail: Same team, same cash left — a completely different idea.
options.storyHeadline: Pivoted to a different idea

gamble.winText: The new direction actually caught on.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Pivoted, and it still didn't work

options.label: Abandon it
options.detail: Wind it down now, before it costs any more.
options.storyHeadline: Shut it down after years with nothing to show

options.label: Keep going
options.detail: One more year to prove it can work.
options.storyHeadline: Kept grinding with nothing to show for it

headline: Market pullback begins
body: Rates are rising and investors are getting cautious everywhere at once. Your own board just called an emergency meeting.

options.label: Cut burn immediately
options.detail: Freeze hiring and slow spending so the cash lasts through whatever's coming.
options.storyHeadline: Tightened belt in uncertain times

options.label: Keep spending through it
options.detail: Everyone else is pulling back. Keep hiring and shipping while they do.
options.storyHeadline: Invested while others retreated

headline: Big tech company tries to poach your team
body: A well-known name is offering your engineers salaries you can't match. One of them has already said yes.

options.label: Raise salaries to match
options.detail: Spend what it takes to keep the rest of the team from following.
options.storyHeadline: Matched offers to retain talent

options.label: Let them go
options.detail: You can't compete on money yet. Wish them well and keep building.
options.storyHeadline: Lost engineer to bigger company

headline: Local currency crashes 30%
body: Your revenue comes in local currency. Your cloud bills are in dollars. Overnight, those bills got a third more expensive.

options.label: Raise prices immediately
options.detail: Protect your margins. Some customers grumble, but the bills still get paid.
options.storyHeadline: Raised prices to survive a currency shock

options.label: Absorb the cost
options.detail: Keep prices exactly where they are and take the hit to your own margin instead.
options.storyHeadline: Took a margin hit for customer loyalty

headline: A smaller, quieter buyout — dressed up as an IPO
body: Your bankers think the market would buy your story, but what they're really offering is a buyout at a rich multiple, paid out as if you'd listed. Tech IPOs are hot right now, and this is the version of that you can actually get.

options.label: Take it and step away
options.detail: Cash out at today's market price and let the company become someone else's story from here.
options.storyHeadline: Took a public-style buyout and stepped away
options.mentorHint: It's priced like a real exit, not a headline number a banker made up. Once you take it, this company is no longer yours to run.

options.label: Wait another year
options.detail: Let the offer go and see if the window is still open next year.
options.storyHeadline: Passed on an early buyout to wait it out
options.mentorHint: Waiting costs nothing today. Windows like this one don't stay open on your schedule.

headline: The money stops
body: Every fund you know has gone quiet. Not "no" — just quiet.

options.label: Cut a third of the staff now
options.detail: Cash lasts much longer. Morale takes a real hit.
options.storyHeadline: Cut staff to survive a funding freeze
options.mentorHint: Cash lasts. So does the fact that the people who stayed watched you decide who didn't.

options.label: Raise at half the price you wanted
options.detail: You give up more than you'd like.
options.storyHeadline: Raised down, but raised
options.mentorHint: You get the round. The price you accepted becomes the price everyone remembers next time.

options.label: Try to survive on revenue alone
options.detail: A real bet on the business as it stands.
options.storyHeadline: Tried to survive the freeze on revenue alone

gamble.winText: You made it, and you own all of it.
gamble.loseText: You ran out with eight months to spare.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Survived the freeze on revenue alone
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Nearly ran out surviving the freeze alone

headline: Everyone is throwing money
body: Three funds have emailed you this week. One offered before seeing a single number.

options.label: Take the biggest cheque
options.detail: Cash to spare. Now you have to grow fast or die.
options.storyHeadline: Took the biggest offer on the table
options.mentorHint: The cheque is real. So is the growth rate they'll now expect every quarter, forever.

options.label: Take a small one at a silly price
options.detail: Barely any dilution.
options.storyHeadline: Took a small round at a great price
options.mentorHint: Barely any dilution — and a board seat you now owe a favour to.

options.label: Take none
options.detail: Feels very smart in two years.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down every offer in a frothy market
options.mentorHint: Nothing's given up today. What it costs only shows up the day you need money and the market's changed its mind.

headline: Your bank fails
body: On a Friday afternoon your bank stops answering. Your payroll is Monday.

options.label: Borrow from an investor personally, overnight
options.detail: Cash is safe. They never let you forget it.
options.storyHeadline: Borrowed overnight to cover a bank failure

options.label: Tell the staff the truth and wait
options.detail: A real gamble on the bank releasing funds.
options.storyHeadline: Waited out a bank failure

gamble.winText: The money was released within a week.
gamble.loseText: You lost a third of it in the chaos.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost cash to a bank failure

options.label: Take an emergency loan at a terrible rate
options.detail: Cash is safe. It costs you for years.
options.storyHeadline: Took an expensive emergency loan

headline: The biggest customer goes bust
body: They owe you four months and they aren't paying anyone.

options.label: Sue
options.detail: Expensive, and a coin flip on getting anything back.
options.storyHeadline: Sued a customer who went bust

gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Got nothing suing a bankrupt customer

options.label: Write it off and move on
options.detail: Revenue takes a hit. You move on.
options.storyHeadline: Wrote off a bankrupt customer

headline: Prices are rising everywhere
body: Everything costs more. Your staff have noticed before you have.

options.label: Raise everyone's pay
options.detail: Costs rise. Morale improves.
options.storyHeadline: Raised pay to keep up with prices

options.label: Raise your prices
options.detail: Revenue holds. You lose some customers.
options.storyHeadline: Raised prices with the market

options.label: Do nothing and hope
options.detail: Two people leave for more money.
options.storyHeadline: Did nothing while prices rose around you

headline: A rival raises an enormous round
body: {RIVAL} just raised more money than you've ever seen. They're hiring your people by Friday.

options.label: Raise too, at any price
options.detail: You get the cash. You give up a lot.
options.storyHeadline: Raised in a hurry to keep pace with a rival
options.mentorHint: You match the raise. You also match their burn rate, with less cash to survive it.

options.label: Compete on being profitable instead
options.detail: Nothing changes now. Matters enormously later.
options.storyHeadline: Chose profitability over matching a rival's raise
options.mentorHint: Nothing changes today. The cost is patience — yours, and everyone watching you not react.

headline: Someone offers to buy you — too early
body: {ACQUIRER} offers a number that would change your life but not your grandchildren's.

options.label: Say no
options.detail: They walk. In a few years you'll know whether that was clever.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down an early acquisition offer

options.label: Ask for double
options.detail: A real bet on your own negotiating position.
options.storyHeadline: Countered an early acquisition offer

gamble.loseText: They walked, and told people you were difficult.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Doubled down on an offer and won
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Pushed too hard on an early offer

headline: The tax bill nobody warned you about
body: An accountant made a mistake three years ago. The government has noticed.

options.label: Pay it
options.detail: One large, clean payment.
options.storyHeadline: Paid an unexpected tax bill in full

options.label: Payment plan
options.detail: Cash lasts, and the company survives.
options.storyHeadline: Put a tax bill on a payment plan

headline: A small round or a big one
body: Two term sheets on the table. One is much bigger than the other, and comes with much bigger expectations attached.

options.label: Take the bigger round
options.detail: More runway, more pressure to grow fast enough to justify it.
options.storyHeadline: Took the big round
options.mentorHint: The number's exciting. So is the growth rate you've now promised to hit.

options.label: Take the smaller round
options.detail: Less cash, less equity given up, less to prove on someone else's timeline.
options.storyHeadline: Took the smaller, careful round
options.mentorHint: Smaller cheque, smaller dilution — and less room if the plan needs more runway than you think.

headline: Turn down the round entirely
body: You don't actually need the money any more.

options.label: Say no to everyone
options.detail: You keep every share you have.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down funding while profitable
options.mentorHint: You keep every share. You also lose the cash cushion for whatever happens next.

options.label: Take it anyway, for speed
options.detail: Cash to move faster, at a real cost.
options.storyHeadline: Took funding anyway, for speed
options.mentorHint: Speed, at a real cost — equity you didn't actually need to give up.

headline: They cut their prices
body: {RIVAL} just went 40% cheaper.

options.label: Match
options.detail: Revenue takes a real hit.
options.storyHeadline: Matched a rival's price cut

options.label: Hold and explain why you're better
options.detail: Lose the price-sensitive customers, keep the rest.
options.storyHeadline: Held prices against a rival's cut

headline: A rival offers to partner
body: Work together on one thing, stay separate otherwise.

options.label: Do it
options.detail: Both of you grow. Some of what they learn is now about you.
options.storyHeadline: Partnered with a rival on one thing

options.label: Decline
options.detail: Nothing.
options.storyHeadline: Declined a rival's partnership offer

headline: A rival is in trouble
body: Word is {RIVAL} is running out of money.

options.label: Hire their people
options.detail: Output climbs.
options.storyHeadline: Hired talent from a struggling rival

options.label: Approach their customers
options.detail: Revenue climbs. You look a little like a vulture.
options.storyHeadline: Went after a struggling rival's customers

options.label: Buy them outright
options.detail: Acquire what's left of them — the team, the customers, all of it.
options.storyHeadline: Bought out a struggling rival outright

headline: Someone new arrives with far more money
body: A well-funded newcomer entering your market.

options.label: Fight
options.detail: Years of an uncertain fight.
options.storyHeadline: Fought a well-funded newcomer

gamble.winText: You held your ground and then some.
gamble.loseText: They out-spent you into a smaller company.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost ground to a well-funded newcomer

options.label: Go somewhere they aren't
options.detail: Smaller for now. Safe.
options.storyHeadline: Moved away from a well-funded newcomer

headline: A bank will lend, if you sign personally
body: Not against the company. Against you.

options.label: Sign it
options.detail: Cash now. The debt is yours if the company can't pay.
options.storyHeadline: Signed a personal guarantee for a bank loan
options.mentorHint: The company's debt usually stays the company's. A personal guarantee quietly changes that.

options.label: Not on those terms
options.detail: The offer stands. You just don't take it.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down a personally-guaranteed loan
options.mentorHint: Nothing happens today. Nothing happens tomorrow either — that's the actual offer.

headline: The bank wants a tighter covenant
body: New terms, mid-loan. They can mostly do this.

options.label: Accept the new terms
options.detail: Reporting, restrictions, a real drag on how you run things.
options.storyHeadline: Accepted a tighter loan covenant

options.label: Pay it off instead
options.detail: Clear the whole balance now and this stops being their business.
options.storyHeadline: Paid off the loan rather than accept a covenant

headline: A second loan, easy to get now
body: You already pay one lender on time. A second one wants in on that.

options.label: Take it too
options.detail: More cash now. Two payments every month from here on.
options.storyHeadline: Took on a second loan
options.mentorHint: The first loan being easy to pay is not evidence the second one will be.

options.label: One is enough
options.detail: Say no while it's still an easy no.
options.storyHeadline: Declined a second loan

headline: Refinancing is on the table
body: Rates have moved since you borrowed. A new lender offers to clear the old loan and write a fresh one.

options.label: Refinance it
options.detail: The old balance disappears into a new loan, priced on who you are today, not who you were.
options.storyHeadline: Refinanced the loan
options.mentorHint: Today's rate might be better. It might not. You won't know which until it's signed.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.detail: The devil you know, on the terms you already agreed to.
options.storyHeadline: Left the loan as it was

headline: A payment is due and cash is tight
body: The loan doesn't care that this is a bad month.

options.label: Find the cash somehow
options.detail: Draw down further to make it on time.
options.storyHeadline: Scraped together a loan payment

options.label: Miss it
options.detail: Keep the cash. Explain it to the bank instead.
options.storyHeadline: Missed a loan payment
options.mentorHint: The fee is the small cost. What a missed payment does to the next loan is the real one.

headline: A lender remembers last time
body: They'll still write the loan. The number they quote makes clear they looked you up first.

options.label: Take it anyway
options.detail: The rate is the rate. It's still cash you don't have otherwise.

effects.holderLabel: A lender who did their homework

options.storyHeadline: Took a loan priced for a founder who'd failed before
options.mentorHint: A worse rate isn't a worse loan. It's the same loan, costing what your record says it should.

options.label: Bootstrap instead
options.detail: Not at that price.
options.storyHeadline: Walked away from a loan priced for a past bankruptcy

headline: You could clear the loan today
body: The cash is sitting right there. So is the balance.

options.label: Pay it off
options.detail: The payments stop. So does the interest.
options.storyHeadline: Paid off the loan early
options.mentorHint: The interest saved is real. So is every other thing that cash could have done instead.

options.label: Keep the cash working
options.detail: The loan is cheap money. Let it keep being cheap money.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the loan running rather than pay it off
